blocks.content: Glaciers form in regions where annual snowfall exceeds melting. Over time, snow compacts into firn and eventually into dense glacial ice.
Glaciers form in regions where annual snowfall exceeds melting.
• Common in polar and high-altitude regions.

items: Correct compaction sequence: Snow compresses into Firn, which then converts into dense Glacial Ice.
Definition of Snowline: It is the lowest altitude where snow persists throughout the entire year.
Latitude Variation: The elevation of the snowline is not constant and varies depending on latitude.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers develop in areas where annual snowfall consistently exceeds snowmelt.
The formation process follows the compaction chain: Snow → Firn → Glacial Ice.
Glacial activity occurs strictly above the snowline in polar and high-altitude regions.
The snowline marks the lowest limit of perpetual snow and fluctuates with latitude.

blocks.content: Snowline is the lowest altitude where snow remains throughout the year. It varies with latitude.
